content.user_title: Map Architecture Before You Change Code
content.value_statement: Complex repositories hide ownership, constraints, and change impact. Birdview builds evidence-linked maps and reviewable implementation scopes before coding begins.
actual_capabilities: Discovers repository instruction files and their linked local references from a committed Git revision.
Builds validated architecture maps with modules, responsibilities, relationships, evidence, and uncertainty markers.
Renders self-contained HTML views for architecture, planned changes, activity, and reviewed constraints.
Links reviewed rules to source ranges, applicability decisions, history, and affected architecture modules.
Prepares a concrete change scope and verification plan before implementation starts.
Supports English, Chinese, and translated map content while preserving identifiers and source paths.
limitations: Maps depend on agent analysis and declared evidence; validation does not prove architectural accuracy.
Constraint discovery focuses on committed Git files and does not automatically include uncommitted or external instructions.
The command-line tools require Node.js 18 or newer, and some workflows also require Git and a browser.
Birdview does not monitor edits automatically or prove that reported checks were executed.

use_cases.title: Understand an unfamiliar repository
use_cases.description: Create an evidence-linked architecture map before selecting files or proposing changes.

use_cases.title: Review an AI change plan
use_cases.description: See affected modules, files, constraints, and verification steps before authorizing implementation.

use_cases.title: Trace repository constraints
use_cases.description: Collect local instructions, review applicability, and connect approved rules to architecture modules.
use_cases.target_user: Maintainers of repositories with layered guidance

prompt_templates.title: Map this repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Birdview to map this repository. Do not edit code. Show the HTML preview, source evidence, coverage, and uncertainties.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner exploration of an unfamiliar project

prompt_templates.title: Review project constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Birdview to discover and review effective constraints for [scope]. Show source coverage, applicability, conflicts, and unresolved gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Constraint inventory for a defined area

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Birdview to plan [change]. Map the current architecture, identify affected modules and files, include applicable constraints, and wait for confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Assess architecture and refactoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Birdview to evaluate [subsystem]. Separate evidence from inference, identify structural risks, propose staged refactoring scopes, and define verification for each stage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture review with phased recommendations

output_examples.input: Map the authentication flow without changing code.
output: An HTML architecture view showing authentication modules and relationships.
Source-linked evidence for each mapped responsibility.
Coverage notes and unresolved architecture questions.

output_examples.input: Plan a cache invalidation change with Birdview.
output: A change view highlighting current and proposed module impact.
A list of affected files, applicable constraints, and verification steps.
A confirmation request before implementation begins.

output_examples.input: Build a complete constraint inventory for the API directory.
output: A reviewed constraint graph grouped by topic and directory.
Source ranges, applicability decisions, and unresolved conflicts.
An explicit statement of checked coverage and remaining gaps.

best_practices: Start with a specific repository scope and state whether you need architecture, constraints, or a change plan.
Review the rendered HTML, evidence links, uncertainty markers, and coverage notes before accepting the map.
Refresh the map when responsibilities, relationships, constraints, or planned modules materially change.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a valid schema as proof that module ownership or architectural claims are correct.
Do not use example maps or unreviewed source text as evidence for the current repository.
Do not start implementation before reviewing and confirming the displayed change scope unless confirmation is explicitly waived.

faq.question: When does Birdview activate?
faq.answer: It activates when explicitly requested, or before coding when the project has configured automatic mode.

faq.question: Does Birdview edit code immediately?
faq.answer: No. It maps and presents the change scope first, then waits for confirmation unless the user explicitly waives that step.

faq.question: What does the architecture map contain?
faq.answer: It contains modules, responsibilities, relationships, source evidence, layout, revision identity, and documented uncertainties.

faq.question: Can Birdview review repository instructions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discover committed instruction files and linked references, then record reviewed applicability and coverage.

faq.question: Does validation guarantee an accurate map?
faq.answer: No. Validation checks structure and consistency. Architectural truth still requires source review and human judgment.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Installation and invocation differ by host.
